metadata.title: SSHSessions
metadata.description: Svendsen Tech's SSH-Sessions module provides SSH session creation, management and interaction from PowerShell. Lets you execute commands via SSH against Linux and certain network equipment, etc. MIT license. Online documentation here: https://www.powershelladmin.com/wiki/SSH_from_PowerShell_using_the_SSH.NET_library

findings.title: Possible hard-coded credential
findings.description: A credential-like variable appears to be assigned a literal value. Review the source; the matched value is redacted.

evidence.snippet: [String] $Password = '[REDACTED]', # I guess allowing for a blank password is "wise"...

findings.title: Plain text is converted to a secure string
findings.description: File 'file-00002.psm1' uses ConvertTo-SecureString with plaintext. This will expose secure information. Encrypted standard strings should be used instead.

findings.title: Separate username and password parameters are declared
findings.description: Function 'New-SshSession' has both Username and Password parameters. Either set the type of the Password parameter to SecureString or replace the Username and Password parameters with a Credential parameter of type PSCredential. If using a Credential parameter in PowerShell 4.0 or earlier, please define a credential transformation attribute after the PSCredential type attribute.

findings.title: Plain text password parameter is declared
findings.description: Parameter '$Password' should not use String type but either SecureString or PSCredential, otherwise it increases the chance to expose this sensitive information.

evidence.snippet: [String] $Password = '[REDACTED]', # I guess allowing for a blank password is "wise"...
